p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines *the problem* that multi-homing a git source across several hosts creates, *the model* that dissolves it (a single-writer mainline with every host as a downstream read-replica), *what the model buys*, *what it costs*, and *how to re-derive* the practice for your own project.

p.sibling-document-pointers: The mechanics of the fan-out live in [`fanout-mechanics.xml`](fanout-mechanics.xml); the maintainer's day-to-day loop in [`daily-loop.xml`](daily-loop.xml).

p.SUPPOSE-THE-PROJECT-MUST-LIVE-ON-TWO-HOS: Suppose the same project must live on two git hosts at once — call them **host A** and **host B**.

facts.REASON-AUDIENCE-PER-HOST: one audience reaches host A and another reaches host B;
facts.REASON-A-HOST-MAY-DISAPPEAR: one host may disappear and the history must survive;
facts.REASON-JURISDICTION-MIRROR-OR-COMMUNITY-: a jurisdiction, a mirror-of-record, or a review community lives on each.

p.BOTH-MUST-CARRY-THE-SAME-HISTORY: Both must always carry the same history, and both are canonical *for reading*.

p.THE-NAIVE-WAY-IS-TO-LET-EACH-ACCEPT-WRIT: The naive way to keep two writable repositories in step is to let each accept writes and mirror to the other.

p.THAT-IS-MULTI-MASTER-REPLICATION: That is **multi-master replication**, and it has one failure mode that never goes away: two independent writes to the same branch **diverge**, and then something must merge them or one must be force-overwritten.

p.EVERY-ADDED-HOST-MULTIPLIES-THE-RACE: Every added host multiplies the race.

p.A-DIVERGENCE-MEANS-CONFLICT-ARCHAEOLOGY-: The moment a divergence appears, a human is doing conflict archaeology on published history — the most expensive kind.

p.THE-FIX-IS-STRUCTURAL-NOT-OPERATIONAL: The fix is structural, not operational.

p.ADOPT-THE-HUB-AND-SPOKE-SHAPE: Adopt the **hub-and-spoke / benevolent-dictator** shape (the Linux-kernel workflow): make mainline **single-writer**, and demote every host to a downstream replica.

mainline.title: Mainline is one local tree; no host is primary

p.MAINLINE-IS-THE-MAINTAINERS-INTEGRATED-L: Mainline is the maintainer's integrated local `main`.

p.MAINLINE-HAS-NO-PRIMARY-HOST: It has **no primary host** — it is not "the host A copy" or "the host B copy"; it is what the maintainer has blessed, replicated equally to every host.

p.ONE-SERIAL-WRITER-MEANS-TWO-WRITES-CANNO: Because exactly one writer advances mainline, and does so **serially**, two divergent writes to `main` cannot race.

p.THE-MULTI-MASTER-PROBLEM-IS-ABSENT-BY-CO: The multi-master problem is **absent by construction, not patched after the fact.**

p.the-cost-of-both-repos-canonical-is-paid: The cost of "both repos canonical" is paid once, in the model, not continuously, in conflict resolution.

replicas.title: Every host is a downstream read-replica

p.EACH-HOST-IS-CANONICAL-FOR-READING-AND-A: Each host is canonical for *reading* in its audience, and a replica for *writing* — nobody writes a target directly.

p.A-DIRECT-WRITE-OR-A-FORCE-PUSH-MAKES-A-T: A direct write to a target, or a force-push, makes it **diverge** from mainline.

p.THE-MODEL-DETECTS-DIVERGENCE-AND-FAILS-L: The model does not paper over that: the tooling detects it and **fails loud** rather than reconciling silently.

p.A-DIVERGED-TARGET-IS-A-SIGNAL-TO-INVESTI: A diverged target is a signal to investigate, never something to clobber.

integration.title: Contributions arrive anywhere; the maintainer integrates

p.A-CHANGE-REACHES-MAINLINE-ONLY-BY-THE-MA: A change reaches mainline only by the maintainer integrating it.

p.PROPOSALS-ARRIVE-HOWEVER-IS-CONVENIENT: Proposals arrive however is convenient — a web PR on host A, a web PR on host B, a branch on a fork, an emailed patch — and are reviewed where they land.

p.ACCEPTING-ONE-MEANS-BRINGING-ITS-COMMITS: Accepting one means bringing its commits into local mainline, then fanning out.

p.THE-WEB-PR-UIS-ARE-INBOXES-NOT-THE-MERGE: The web PR UIs are *inboxes and review surfaces, not the merge authority*.

p.this-is-exactly-the-kernels-workflow: This is exactly the kernel's "patches by email, integrated in the maintainer's tree, pushed to a hub that mirrors out" — the web UIs are merely nicer inboxes than a mailing list.

facts.BUYS-DIVERGENCE-IS-IMPOSSIBLE-BY-CONSTRU: **Divergence is impossible by construction.** One serial writer means no two writes to `main` can race. There is no reconciliation step to get wrong because there is no concurrent write to reconcile.
facts.BUYS-ANY-HOST-CAN-VANISH-WITHOUT-DATA-LO: **Any host can vanish without data loss.** Every host holds the full history of the refs the manifest declares for it; mainline holds the whole tree. A host going dark, getting blocked, or deleting the repo costs a line in the manifest, not a commit.
facts.BUYS-AUDIENCE-AND-JURISDICTION-PER-HOST: **Audience and jurisdiction per host.** Each host serves its own region, community, or compliance surface, while all serve identical history. Adding a host is one manifest entry.
facts.BUYS-THE-INVARIANT-IS-RUNNABLE-CAPITAL: **The invariant is runnable capital.** "Never `--force`" is not a prose promise — it is pinned by a test over the push command ([`fanout-mechanics.xml` §never-force-test](fanout-mechanics.xml#never-force-test)).

p.ONE-HUMAN-SERIALIZES-EVERY-MERGE: Be honest about the bottleneck: **one human serializes every merge.**

p.MAINLINE-ADVANCES-ONLY-AS-FAST-AS-THE-MA: Mainline advances only as fast as the maintainer integrates.

p.there-is-no-parallel-write-path: There is no parallel write path — that is the whole point, and it is also the whole cost.

td.ROW-COST-FAILURE-SURFACE-SINGLE-WRITER-M: A loud abort before any harm

p.for-a-small-team-the-trade-is-strongly-p: For a **small-team or single-maintainer project**, the trade is strongly positive: integration is not the throughput limit (review and design are), and the maintainer was serializing the important merges anyway.

p.THE-MODEL-MAKES-SERIALIZATION-THE-ONLY-W: The model just makes that serialization the *only* write path, so nothing can sneak around it and diverge.

p.when-a-project-outgrows-one-integrator-t: When a project outgrows one integrator — several full-time committers merging in parallel all day — this model is the wrong tool, and the honest answer is to add one-directional server-side mirroring or move to a shared-forge workflow.

p.RECORD-THAT-AS-A-REVISIT-TRIGGER: Record that as a revisit trigger, not a someday-maybe.

re-derive.title: Re-derive for your project

p.re-derive-lead: Do not copy the host names or the script verbatim — copy the *task*, and let the agent derive the setup your project actually needs:

re-derive.fence: Read this flow's documents (your project installed them — typically `vibedeps/flow-source-mirrors/<version>/spec/flows/source-mirrors/`, check `vibe.lock`) in full, then adapt it to this project: 1. List every git host this source must live on, and for each: is it a push target (we push to it) or self-mirroring (it pulls itself)? 2. Name the single mainline — the one local tree that is the merge authority. Confirm no host is treated as primary today; if one is, say so. 3. Draft the target manifest: one entry per host (name, url, mode, refs). No credentials in it — those stay in the maintainer's keys. 4. Adapt the reference fan-out script to that manifest, keeping it fast-forward-only with NO --force path, and add the invariant check (a test or a CI grep) that proves --force can never be emitted. 5. Show me the manifest and the script as diffs. Apply nothing until I approve, and never push to a host as part of this exercise.

facts.SUM-MULTI-HOMING-INVITES-DIVERGENCE-AND-: Multi-homing across hosts invites multi-master divergence; this model dissolves it instead of managing it.
facts.SUM-WHAT-IT-BUYS: What it buys: divergence impossible by construction, any host can vanish without data loss, audience/jurisdiction per host.
facts.SUM-WHAT-IT-COSTS: What it costs: one human serializes merges. Acceptable — and cheaper than the alternative — for small-team projects; record a revisit trigger for the day it is not.
facts.SUM-THE-NEVER-FORCE-INVARIANT-IS-RUNNABL: The never-`--force` invariant is runnable capital, not a promise.
